body:
I've added `$$type` to the middleware to distinguish middlwares.
Not sure about the prefix `aism.` though.
`insights` middleware needs to have something extra. What do you think of the usage of generic here? Any better way to achieve it?
I think `ais` is good enough

I think this should be added to InstantSearch directly

```
instantsearch.middlewareGrabBag.insights.SendEvent = ...
```

or even directly:

```
instantsearch.$insights.sendEvent
```

Maybe that's less easily typeable though
This doesn't seem like the most efficient method, I think it should be added to an object instead of an array
this probably should be called directly from the widgets, without a builtin method for insights in the InstantSearch API
I've changed it to `this._insightsMiddleware.sendEvent()`

`instantSearchInstance.sendEventToInsights()` will be mostly called from connectors.
(For example, [here](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/feat/send-events/src/connectors/refinement-list/connectRefinementList.js#L308-L312) -> [here](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/feat/send-events/src/lib/utils/createSendEventForFacet.ts#L19:L19))

And we can guide users to use it when they want to send a custom event.
So I've exposed `sendEventToInsights()` in InstantSearch as a public method.
What do you think?

(I've updated the summary of this PR. You can scroll to the top and read the summarized version.)
I think this code should be _inside_ the middleware

It makes sense, this way the widgets can assume the middleware exists, even if it doesn't. 

We have a similar thing with createURL returning a default of `#`

I thought a little, but can't think of a way to share this default value efficiently. The downside I see here is that if someone wants to make their own middleware which is optional, they need to add some code to InstantSearch
Could we maybe do something like `instantsearchInstance.sendEvent?()` (which gets called in the widget directly, after being added to the instance by the middleware)
this error needs to be smaller in prod IMO

I think this use case fits us good enough, but it means that if there are two refinement lists on the same attribute, one disjunctive, one conjunctive, the isFacetRefined will be wrong.

However, this should be checked, since maybe it's not possible at all to mix
is this still needed?

> The downside I see here is that if someone wants to make their own middleware which is optional, they need to add some code to InstantSearch

I agree. Potentially we could have `instantSearchInstant.middlewareBlahBlah` as a hub to access middlewares or things returned/added by middlewares. I think you left this idea as a comment somewhere in this PR or the other.

For now, I like your idea [here](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4456#discussion_r462103344). I'll try that.
I love this idea. It makes so many verbose things disappear. https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4456/commits/19751711777f8621e483d5d4a33ada728f938ae6
not anymore https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4456/commits/19751711777f8621e483d5d4a33ada728f938ae6
done https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4456/commits/19751711777f8621e483d5d4a33ada728f938ae6
I actually wanted to discuss. Should this be an exception? Or just a warning to dev?

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/499898/88784472-5fbdee00-d190-11ea-9875-e190743dc1fa.png)

okay it's not possible at all at least at the moment.
We want insights probably not to be an error in production, but maybe an error in dev can make sense
Okay, it makes sense. I'll throw errors with `__DEV__` condition.

I stringified `facetValue` because the value could contain special characters like double qoutes.
Is it enough? I think we should have similar logic somewhere in either InstantSearch, helper or client.
I haven't looked into them yet.
If someone already knows, can you point me to it?
What needs to receive this formatted? Is this for the js client or something else?

It's not for the js client. The [doc](https://www.algolia.com/doc/api-reference/api-methods/clicked-filters/#method-param-filters) refers to `filters` in the api reference. So I thought I should follow the `filters` format which requires the value to be quoted when it's with a space or quotes, etc.
Since users are meant to create their own middleware, I think `$$type` should be optional.
We can reuse `this.$$type`.

The `sendEvent` and `bindEvent` function references are lost between `init` and `render` because they're reassigned. This means that if users bind an event callback in `init` (when `isFirstRender` is true), the callback will be a noop even during `render` (when `isFirstRender` is false).

You can see how we usually fix this by searching for `connectorState` in the codebase.
